chunks: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'Incumbent upon you is supplication, for supplication to Allah and seeking from Allah repels the affliction even after it has been pre-determined and decreed, with nothing remaining but its execution. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is supplicated and asked, He turns away the affliction with a complete turning away.'

key_terms.إِمْضَاء: imda' — execution, ratification; the final stage of divine decree coming into effect
key_terms.الدُّعَاء: du'a — supplication; the act of calling upon Allah with humility and need
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: bala' — affliction, trial, tribulation sent as a test or punishment
key_terms.قُدِّرَ وَقُضِيَ: pre-determined and decreed — two stages of divine fate (qadar and qada)

ai.seo_question: Can supplication (du'a) change or repel a decreed affliction in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) urges his followers to engage persistently in supplication (du'a), affirming that it has the power to repel divinely decreed afflictions. This teaching addresses a theological concern common in Islamic thought: if fate is pre-ordained, can prayer change it? The Imam resolves this by teaching that du'a is itself built into the divine economy — it is the mechanism through which Allah averts calamity even after it has been written.
